name: burnside

phase_0.boundary_condition: The free Burnside group B(m,n) defined by the presentation <S | x^n = 1>

VINIT.justification: The identity element e before any generators are applied to the tape.

TANCH.justification: The terminal boundary that reduces all words to their canonical form in the group.

AFWD.justification: The forward morphism appending a generator to the current word.

AREV.justification: The reverse morphism appending the inverse of a generator.

CLINK.justification: The composition of two word segments into a single sequence.

IMSCRIB.justification: Self-recognition of whether a word reduces to the empty word e.

FSPLIT.justification: Splits a word into alternating periodic segments and aperiodic bridges.

FFUSE.justification: Interleaves bridges and periodic segments to recover the original word.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation that periodic segments satisfy the group exponent.

EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation detecting obstructions to finiteness in bridges.

ENGAGR.justification: Holds the state where B(m,n) is simultaneously finite and infinite for unresolved n.

IFIX.justification: Permanent record of the proven finiteness or infiniteness of the group.

phase_3.void_description: uninitialized word tape with no generators
phase_3.true_description: finite group status where the word problem is decidable
phase_3.false_description: infinite group status with elements of infinite order
phase_3.both_description: unresolved paradox where finiteness is neither proven nor refuted

steps.domain_action: initialize the word tape to the identity element e
append generator a1 to the tape
append inverse generator a2⁻¹ to the tape
concatenate the current tape with a seed word segment
apply Burnside reduction x^n=1 to the entire tape
decompose the reduced word into periodic runs and aperiodic bridges
verify that all periodic runs are locally finite under exponent n
check bridges for aperiodic residuals that indicate infinite order
reconstruct the original word from the Adian components to ensure integrity
test if the reconstructed word is equivalent to the identity e
engage the paradox register for the specific exponent n
permanently fix the status based on Novikov-Adian or Burnside theorems
perform final self-recognition to close the proof protocol

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The word rewriting system applying free and Burnside reductions
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Tuple-based word passing between reduction and decomposition functions
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The state dictionary storing the word tape and history
phase_5.alfs_store: The classification table of known finite and infinite exponents

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational cycles required for O(|w|³) word reduction
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A word of length L in the free group
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A reduced word of length L' <= L in the Burnside group
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The reduction is a deterministic mapping to a canonical form
